title: The web UI for buyer and approver

events.text: The web UI for buyer and approver
events.body: ## Goal Four server-rendered pages — buyer list, draft editor, requisition detail with its history, and the approver queue — that make the rule, the amount and the reason visible before and after a decision. ## Context Part of #6. Builds on split 3: the same HTTP API, the same typed refusals, the same `OrgScope`. The UI is a client of the API, not a second implementation of the rules. Honor D-013 (server-rendered HTML from small template functions + a ~50-line vanilla-JS `fetch` helper; **no framework, no bundler, no build step**; one hand-written stylesheet served static; all output through one `esc()` helper — templates take data, never raw HTML; the demo token is entered once and kept in `sessionStorage`, never in a URL, a log or a query string), D-012 (the same `node:http` router serves the pages and the static assets), D-016 (a refusal is rendered as a human sentence carrying its stable `code`; a cross-org id shows the same "not found" page as an unknown id), D-010 (the client generates an `Idempotency-Key` per user action — a submit/approve/reject button press — and reuses it on retry, so a double-click is one state change), D-003 (amounts always rendered with their currency via `formatMoney`; never a bare number), D-009 (a rejection form requires a reason before it will submit; a rejected requisition offers "copy to a new draft", not "reopen"), D-007 (the detail page renders the audit history verbatim: actor, action, rule, amount, timestamp, reason). **Do NOT**: add React/Vue/Svelte/htmx or any npm package; add a bundler or a CSS framework; put the token in a URL or a cookie without `HttpOnly`/`SameSite` reasoning written in the PR; re-implement rule matching or authority checks in the browser (ask the API, render the answer); build HTML by string concatenation of untrusted values or use `innerHTML` with server data; hide a refusal behind a generic "something went wrong". Pages: `GET /` (redirect by role) · `/requisitions` (buyer list, filter by state) · `/requisitions/new` and `/requisitions/:id/edit` (draft editor: catalogue picker, quantity, cost centre, note, live computed total and the rule that would match) · `/requisitions/:id` (detail + history + the action buttons the actor is actually allowed) · `/approvals` (the approver queue, oldest first, with amount and matched rule per row). New rows: none reserved. A `D-` row is expected only if the token-handling choice in the browser needs to differ from D-013 — in which case write it, do not quietly diverge. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The four routes render valid HTML with no JavaScript required for every **read** path; a test asserts the detail and queue pages render fully with the client script removed. - [ ] The draft editor shows the computed total and the rule that would match, updating when a line or quantity changes, and a test asserts the displayed rule equals the API's answer for the same input (no second implementation). - [ ] Escaping: a requisition note, an item name and a rejection reason each containing `` and `">

feat(web): the buyer and approver pages - server-rendered HTML, one esc(), a cookie session (#4, D-025)
The web UI for buyer and approver — server-rendered pages, one esc(), a cookie session (#4, D-025)
events.body: Closes #4 ## Summary Four server-rendered pages on the same `node:http` router, the same origin and the same use cases as the JSON API: the buyer list (`/requisitions`, filterable by state), the draft editor (`/requisitions/new`, `/requisitions/:id/edit` — catalogue picker, quantity, cost centre, note, and the server's running total plus the rule that would match), the requisition detail with its audit history and the actions this caller may actually take, and the approver queue (`/approvals`, oldest wait first). New code lives in `src/web/`; the only change outside it is a six-line mount in `src/http/app.ts` that hands every non-`/api/` path to `handleWeb` — the JSON surface, including its single `not_found` mapping, is byte-for-byte what it was. Nothing re-implements a rule: the handlers call `createDraft`/`submit`/`approve`/`reject`/ `cancel`/`copyForward` from `src/app/requisitions.ts`, render `actions` for the buttons and `matchRule` (server-side) for the editor's preview. Every value goes through one `esc()`. The ~50 lines of vanilla JS do exactly two things — ask `POST /requisitions/preview` for the total and the rule and set them with `textContent`, and stop a second submit — and every **read** path renders fully without them. Zero runtime dependencies, no bundler, no build step; the stylesheet and the client script are source constants served from `/static/` (`tsc` emits `.js` only, so a `.css` under `src/` would simply not exist in `dist/`). **D-025 amends D-013's `sessionStorage` clause** (the issue anticipated exactly this row). A browser navigation carries no `Authorization` header, so a page that must read without JavaScript cannot be authenticated from `sessionStorage`. The session is therefore the same personal token in an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` cookie, `Secure` off localhost, set by a `POST /sign-in` form and never rendered again — resolved by the same `verifyToken` → `resolveScope` pair, so there is no second identity mechanism and no session store. `HttpOnly` is *stronger* than `sessionStorage` (script cannot read the token at all); `SameSite=Strict` plus a `Sec-Fetch-Site` check on every mutating page route is the CSRF answer, alongside `form-action 'self'` and the required `version`. Pages also carry `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; …`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Cache-Control: no-store`; `nosniff` was already global. Each form carries the `Idempotency-Key` the server rendered into it, so a double-click, a reload of the POST or a retry is one state change — with **or without** JavaScript — through the same D-010 ledger the API uses (a `303` stores its `Location`, anything else stores the page). ## Evidence for the reviewers **Board, all green** (`npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run lint && check-anchors.mjs && render.mjs --check`): typecheck clean · **434 tests, 434 pass, 0 fail** (~5.5 s) · lint clean · anchors `25 D · 21 G · 10 M rows, every reference resolves` · framework `19 generated files match`. 30 files, +3 177 / −3. New suites in `test/web/` (25 tests): `walkthrough` 2 · `escaping` 3 · `no-js` 3 (incl. the accessibility floor) · `authority` 6 · `idempotency` 5 · `money` 4 · `session` 6 · `preview` 3. Everything runs in-process through `dispatch` with no listening port, offline, `:memory:` (D-014). **Mutations — seven tried, seven went red:** | # | Mutation | What went red | |---|---|---| | 1 | `esc()` stops escaping `"` | `escaping`: the raw `">` through every template that takes free text — line note, item name, cost centre name, person name, organisation name, rejection reason, and the refusal sentence that quotes the input — asserting raw-absent **and** escaped-present each time) · authority (button absent **and** direct POST `not_authorised`, for the wrong approver and for the buyer's own requisition) · rejection needs a reason (`required` in the markup *and* the server's `validation_failed`, with the requisition still on screen) · double-click (`idempotency.test.ts` fires the identical form twice and counts versions and audit lines; a companion assertion shows a *different* key on the same version refuses, so the replay is doing the work) · currency on every amount (a scan of every `` on every page, with a presence counter so the scan cannot pass by finding nothing) · JPY renders no decimals and refuses a decimal rather than rounding it · no token in any URL, log line or page source (`session.test.ts` captures `process.stdout`/`stderr` over a full walkthrough with the log at `info` and greps the captured output — with a presence assertion that the walkthrough really was logged) · `npm ci` installs no runtime dependency (the existing `package-shape` suite already fails on one) and no build step was added. **Deviations** 1. **The "note" is per line, not per requisition.** The issue's editor names a "note"; the schema (D-023/#3) has no requisition-level note column and this PR adds no migration (and would have collided with #5). The editor's free-text field is the line `description`, labelled "Note — what this line is for". Written up as **G-021** with its trigger, not left silent. 2. **A `D-` row was needed** — D-025, as the issue anticipated. Rationale above and in the row. 3. **`parseAmountMinor`/`amountField` live in `src/web/amount.ts`, not in `src/domain/money.ts`.** They are form-field parsing (the inverse of `formatMoney`), and the instruction for this split was to keep changes inside `src/web/`. No rounding happens in them — a third EUR decimal or any JPY decimal is refused, so D-003's single rounding function stays uncalled. 4. **Adding a line without JavaScript** is "the editor always renders one blank spare row", not a JS-only "add line" button. Cheapest thing that keeps the no-JS path whole. 5. **`/` redirects a buyer to `/requisitions` and everybody else to `/approvals`** — the issue says "redirect by role" without naming the tie-break for somebody holding both. ## Docs - **D-025** (new) — the page session cookie, with the attribute-by-attribute rationale and five rejected alternatives; **addendum to D-013** recording that its `sessionStorage` clause is superseded and that everything else in the row is built as written. - **G-020** (new) — the residual: the cookie *is* the bearer token, so signing out clears only this browser's copy. Trigger: G-013 being answered, or the first deployment outside the demo. - **G-021** (new) — the missing requisition-level note, with the trigger that reopens it. - `docs/08-security.md` — new **T11** (CSRF on the pages) with its stated residual; **T5** and **T7** extended with the cookie, the CSP and the escaping table test. - `README.md` — a "The pages" section after the route table (deliberately *not* the quickstart section, which #5 owns). - Nothing else was made wrong by this change. ## Dependencies None. `dependencies` stays empty and `devDependencies` stays at the three D-001 names; the existing `package-shape` suite enforces both. ## Audit contribution No new audit shape: every state change a page makes goes through the same `src/app/` use cases, inside the same `withTransaction`, so the existing D-007 line (actor, action, from/to state, rule, total + currency, reason, request id) is written unchanged — this PR's contribution is that the detail page now **renders** that history verbatim: actor name, action, state edge, rule code, amount with its currency, timestamp and reason. ## Manual steps Only a person with a browser can confirm the parts a string assertion cannot: 1. `REQUISIT_TOKEN_SECRET=<32+ bytes> npm start`, open `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`, sign in with a minted token (`npm run mint-token`). Check DevTools → Application → Cookies: `requisit_session` shows **HttpOnly ✓, SameSite Strict**, and `document.cookie` in the console returns `""`. 2. Draft a requisition: pick a catalogue item and leave the note and price empty — they fill from the catalogue row on save. Type in the quantity field and watch the total and the rule line update without a page load; then **switch JavaScript off** and confirm "Recalculate" does the same thing and that the detail and queue pages still read completely. 3. Double-click **Submit** and then **Approve** hard, and confirm one state change and one history line each (with JS off too — the hidden key is what does it, not the button guard). 4. Reject with a reason and confirm the buyer sees it verbatim, that the offer is "Copy to a new draft" and never "Reopen", and that the page is legible at phone width. 5. Sign out and press Back: the page must not come from the cache (`Cache-Control: no-store`). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

🔨 Implemented in draft PR #9 — https://github.com/FRZWLF/requisit/pull/9

Board green (typecheck · 434 tests · lint · anchors · framework render). 30 files, +3 177 / −3.
New rows: **D-025** (the page session cookie, amending D-013's `sessionStorage` clause, as this issue anticipated), **G-020** (the residual: the cookie is the bearer token), **G-021** (no requisition-level note — the editor's free text is the line description). `docs/08-security.md` gains **T11** (CSRF on the pages).

## 🧪 Quality review Board re-run in a clean worktree off `feat/issue-4`: `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run lint && check-anchors.mjs .` — **434 tests, 434 pass, 0 fail**, lint and typecheck clean, anchors `25 D · 21 G · 10 M rows, every reference resolves`. Every `D-`/`G-` reference the diff adds (D-003, D-004, D-005, D-006, D-008, D-009, D-010, D-012, D-013 + addendum, D-016, D-018, D-021, D-023, D-024, **D-025**, G-013, **G-020**, **G-021**, T5/T7/**T11**) has a row, and the D-013 addendum correctly records which clause is superseded rather than leaving the old row lying. Two mutations of my own, neither on the PR's list of seven: 1. `detailPage`'s `keyFor` made to return one fixed key for every action on a page (the code comment claims two buttons must not share a key) → **red**, 2 tests in `idempotency`. The comment is load-bearing and pinned. 2. Not a mutation but a probe, because the security brief asks about cross-org through the pages: two organisations seeded into **one** database (the shipped test uses two), then org A's buyer against org B's requisition — detail `404` with the body byte-identical to an unknown id, B's item text absent from A's list, B's cost centre absent from A's editor, and a hand-crafted POST naming B's cost centre refused `404`, not `303`. **Cross-org holds on the page surface.** On the rest of the security brief: the cookie carries `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` with `Secure` added off localhost and a `COOKIE_SAFE` guard before it is ever set (`src/web/session.ts`); `sameSiteOk` runs in `handleWeb` **before** auth and before any handler, so it covers every `POST` page route including `/sign-in` and `/sign-out`; the CSP is `default-src 'none'` with `form-action 'self'` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`, and I found no inline `style=`, no inline `
fix(web): the edit action is a styled link, not a button inside an anchor (review nit)

## 📋 Pipeline (in-chat) — issue #4 → PR #9 → `7a7ad57`

| stage | model | outcome | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| triage | haiku | blocked on #3 (first pass) · area:web · size:M · risk:medium · pipeline:build (second pass) | 69932 |
| architect | — | not run (size:M) | — |
| implement | opus | draft PR #9 — 3 177 lines, 434 tests, 7 mutations red; D-025 (cookie session) written because D-013's sessionStorage clause cannot serve no-JS pages | 213897 |
| quality review (with the security brief) | opus | findings (0 red, 5 nits) — cookie flags, CSRF, CSP, esc() all verified | 115302 |
| fix loop | — | none needed | — |
| gate | orchestrator | one-liner nit fixed (anchor-wrapped button → styled link); four multi-file nits → follow-up #11; board green on branch and on `main` (typecheck · 434/434 · lint · anchors 25 D · 21 G · 10 M · render 19 files) | — |
| **total** | | | **399131** |

**Reviews found:** nothing red. The security questions in the brief (HttpOnly/SameSite cookie, Sec-Fetch-Site guard, CSP, one esc() on every value, no authority in the pages, cross-org 404) all held. Nits: a cross-org test that used two databases, invalid HTML, the Secure flag decided from Host, HTML pages in the idempotency ledger, problem+json on a page throw.

**Decisions:** D-025 cookie session (implementer's D-row, as the issue anticipated); G-020 sign-out semantics; G-021 no requisition-level note. PR assigned to FRZWLF for the after-the-fact review.

**Manual steps left for FRZWLF:** the browser walkthrough in the PR body (cookie flags in DevTools, JS-off flow, double-click submit/approve, back button after sign-out).

**Follow-ups:** #11.
